title: Launching Writer’s Workshop in Kinder and First Grade- Narrative Mini-lesson
description:
This writing workshop lesson was adapted from the Kinder Unit 1 session: We Are All Writers and the 1st Grade Unit 1 session: Lives Are Full of Stories to Tell.  
 
This writing workshop video was taped on the sixth day of school with a classroom full of eager, bright-eyed 1st graders who have never implemented the workshop structure before.  It always seems a little nerve wrecking to launch so much information in the very beginning of the year, much less the very first days of school… because it feels as though the students will have trouble processing the mini-lesson.  But we should know that students will always thrive and approximate the best they can.  We must change their mindset of “I can’t, it’s too hard, I’ll never get it...” to “I can, it’s not that hard, and I’ll keep trying the best that I can!”

Everyone was pleased to see the students choose different topics to write about and go off to try it at their desks.

title: Shared Reading Day 1
description: This shared reading video takes place in Ms. Manor's 1st grade classroom using the story, "Flora's Blanket." Shared Reading is a great time to bring the students to the carpet for a short amount of time (10 minutes) and have everyone's eyes on one text. Each day is focused on a specific reading foundational skill and reading literature standard. As I introduce the book, I want to emphasize how we are using the pictures FIRST by looking at the cover, back of the book, title, and even the title page to "get our brains ready" before we even start reading the book.  We are doing inferential work by looking at the pictures and thinking how the characters are feeling as they go on this adventure to search for Flora's blanket.  The students are highly engaged and have started to change their voices to match the character in the text because of the repetition.  Awesome class!!!

title: 1st Grade Writing Workshop Lesson- Editing in Opinion Writing
description:
This writing workshop lesson was adapted from the 1st grade UOS Session 12: Partners Work Together to Give Writing Checkups! 

The 1st graders are getting ready to celebrate their opinion pieces this week and are revising and editing their work to prepare for the celebration.  The partnership work directly supports the Common Core Language Standards (with editing/conventions) and the Speaking and Listening standards which ask students to participate in collaborative conversations and clarify something that is not understood.  

I chose to model this work with my own demonstration piece which contained many of the similar mistakes you would find in your student's work.  My teaching point was to show writers "an important part of this process is to be thorough, moving down the page and across the piece, checking that each and every part is the best it can be- teaching young writers to slow down rather than hastily marking off their editing checklist." (pg. 91 Session 12)  I did not state each part of the mini-lesson with the exact wording from Lucy Calkins- but I hope each part of the mini-lesson is noticeable with my transitions. 

Connection:  A story about going to the doctor's office for a thorough checkup and connecting how thorough the doctor was to that of a writing checklist/partner. 

Teaching Point:  Students can be writing doctors and help their partners by...using an editing checklist to make sure your partner's piece is easy to read and the best it can be.

Teach:  Reviewing the teacher's opinion writing using the checklist/chart "Writers Edit and Fix Mistakes" or "How Did I Make My Writing Easy to Read?" (chart from the unit)  Providing a demonstration of what I would like them to try next.

Active Engagement:  Students get a chance to practice with a partner using the editing checklist.

Link:  Remember to be like a writing doctor and go part by part with the editing checklist to make sure your work or your partner's work is the best it can be!

title: Guided Reading Kindergarten- Level C
description:
During this guided reading session, the students will be working on an instructional level C book.  

Using Fountas and Pinnell's Literacy Continuum, they state the features of a level B text consists of two lines of print, patterned language, and supportive illustrations.  Now, in my guided reading lesson, I wanted to support the students in the 'new' type of book they'll be reading (level C) by providing a little bit of a text level introduction along with supporting them with the oral language that's in the text.  I felt this was important since they've been in level B for a few months now and they are used to patterned language on every page.  

We have been working on characters and character traits during interactive read aloud so it's always great to bring in that work during guided reading so students continuously think about, "how the character is feeling...and why? What kind of person/character is he/she?"

title: Immersion in Writing Workshop:  Using a Checklist
description:
We all know the importance of immersing our students- especially when we are changing genres/text types and the students have been writing in one area of text for a long period of time.  Immersion happens the week before you introduce the genre/text type with read alouds, shared writing, and exemplar pieces.  

The kindergarten class is starting their opinion writing unit and I'm introducing how the checklist is used and the purpose of using one.  The many complaints I hear from teachers and even with my own students is that the checklist turns into something that the students literally just "check" off and don't take the time to check their pieces to make sure they've included everything in their piece.
